content.content:
This function call is incorrect because the event_id should be the actual ID of the event, not the name of the event. To reschedule an event, you would need to know its ID. 

Here is a corrected version of the function call:

```
{"name": "reschedule_calendar_event", "parameters": {"event_id": "12345", "new_start_time": "2024-05-20 10:00"}}
```

Replace "12345" with the actual ID of your "Dental check-up" event. 

Also, note that the new_end_time parameter is optional. If you want to keep the same duration for the event, you can omit this parameter and the function will automatically calculate the new end time based on the new start time. If you want to specify a new end time, you can add it as a third parameter. For example:

```
{"name": "reschedule_calendar_event", "parameters": {"event_id": "12345", "new_start_time": "2024-05-20 10:00", "new_end_time": "2024-05-20 11:00"}}
```
